public_rationale: Alphabet reported 2025 GAAP revenue of $402.836 billion and net income of $132.170 billion, close to the quoted amounts [e1]. At June 30, 2026, Alphabet reported $242.5 billion in cash, equivalents and short-term marketable securities; Anthropic reported approximately $131.7 billion in cash, equivalents and short-term investments, excluding restricted cash [e2, e3]. These balances establish greater liquidity for Alphabet, but do not settle the undefined comparison 'vastly more' [e2, e3]. The OpenAI report gives only a lower bound of more than $73 billion at March 31, 2026, leaving the required June comparison unresolved [e4].
limitations: The claim's accounting basis and rounding method are unspecified. The reported revenue rounds to $403 billion to the nearest billion; the evidence does not establish how Marcus obtained $402 billion [e1].
No comparable June 30, 2026 OpenAI balance was verified; the March report is secondary reporting [e4].
The contract supplies no numerical threshold for 'vastly'; comparisons require consistent treatment of securities, restricted cash and debt.
Anthropic's June balances became public on October 26, 2026, after the August 6 statement [e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Google made $402 billion revenue and $132 billion profit last year and has vastly more cash than OpenAI and Anthropic.

statement.excerpt: Google still makes a ton of money, $402 billion in revenue last year, $132 billion in profit), and has vastly more cash to play with than OpenAI and Anthropic.
statement.document_title: Seven reasons I wouldn’t count Google out

from_speaker: vastly more cash to play with than OpenAI and Anthropic
our_interpretation: Google means consolidated Alphabet, consistent with the post's interchangeable use of Google and Alphabet.
Last year means calendar 2025. Profit ordinarily means net income. The figures are approximate whole-billion descriptions, although the revenue rounding is unspecified.
The current cash comparison concerns the latest completed reporting quarter before publication, ending June 30, 2026.
Cash to play with ordinarily includes unrestricted cash, cash equivalents and readily marketable short-term investments. Financing announcements and future operating earnings are not cash balances.
The target interval encompasses two distinct components: 2025 annual results and the June 2026 cash snapshot. They must be tested separately.
No source or accounting basis is attributed in the supplied words. The contract therefore retains an unknown accounting basis rather than inferring GAAP from the evidence.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable financial records establish approximately the stated 2025 revenue and net income, and contemporaneous cash resources substantially exceeding those of each named competitor.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records materially disagree with either annual figure, or establish that Alphabet's available cash resources were comparable to or below those of either competitor.

In addition, we had $2.5 billion of restricted cash primarily

due to amounts held as collateral for our lease and other obligations.
evidence.locator: Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk — Interest Rate Risk; Liquidity and Capital Resources
evidence.explanation: The surrounding disclosure reports $112.4 billion in cash and equivalents and $19.3 billion in short-term investments, separately from restricted cash. That is substantial liquidity and makes the strength of the word 'vastly' material.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An identified source and accounting basis for the annual figures, comparable June 30, 2026 liquidity records for all three companies, and a justified interpretation of 'vastly more' would allow the combined claim to be settled.
